Demonstrate understanding of engineering and technological processes by accessing information relevant to managing and utilising water resources.
Use critical thinking to analyse the impact and implications of engineering issues in the context of sustainable and ethical management of water resources.
Identify how managing water resources may be influenced by socio-economic, cultural, organisational and political factors and requires critical engagement with the latest research and practice.
Identify current issues affecting managing water resources
Demonstrate understanding by explaining the processes used to manage surface water resources

title: Design of Roads and Drainage
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:James Ghent (jghent@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Explain, describe and apply theory of surveying and road design
Apply practical knowledge and skills in the design of roads and drainage systems for sub-developments
Produce engineering designs and plans and conduct engineering investigations as a result of collaboration with others in a team project environment

title: Engineering Research Methodology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Helen Fairweather (hfairwea@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Apply current knowledge of quantitative and qualitative methods used in engineering research.
Analyse, interpret and evaluate data that relate to complex theoretical and technical engineering problems.
Communicate complex research results to specialist audiences.
Act professionally, autonomously and in teams to produce a professional product.

title: Engineering Project 2
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Christophe Gerber (cgerber@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Apply the Engineering Process to conduct an engineering project.
Challenge engineering practice and contribute to new developments in your engineering discipline.
Define a problem and formulate a problem statement.
Review, engage and challenge the (research) literature in a specialist domain / an engineering discipline.
Develop and design concepts, solutions and procedures in your engineering discipline.
Test and evaluate your concepts, solutions and procedures to reach informed decisions.
Reflect on and evaluate the project impacts for the community (e.g. engineering discipline) and environment.
Manage your project incl. planning, organising and managing resources and prioritising competing demands.
Communicate about your project, its development and outcomes to a professional audience in several media.
Work collaboratively in a project team.

title: Design of Water Supply Systems
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Peter Schwammberger (pschwamm@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Understand engineering and technological processes by accessing information relevant to managing water supply
Access and evaluate information regarding managing water supply and treatment sustainably
Explain and understand the processes used to manage water supply and treatment and the socio-economic and environmental factors that influence it
Discuss the implications of and outcomes from inappropriate application of engineering principles in managing water supply and treatment
Illustrate a possible solution to a water supply and treatment problem or illustrate how engineering may be causing the problem

title: Engineering Project Management Principles
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Examine modern project management theory and demonstrate relevant practice techniques.
Evaluate alternative approaches to managing projects and identify optimal solutions to meet complex contextual demands in different sectors.
Apply project management tools and processes to the scoping, planning and execution of an engineering project and monitoring of progress and performance.
Apply acquisition strategies and participate constructively, as a member of a multi-disciplinary engineering team, in the selection of consultants, contractors and resources.
Judge key issues in management systems and control with regard to quality management and WHS.
Evaluate the social, environmental, and economic principles, norms and accountabilities of sustainable engineering practice in engineering project management.

title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Adrian McCallum (amccallu@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Apply current practical and theoretical knowledge of fundamental geotechnical engineering principles, concepts and technologies that relate to building structures on soil in regional contexts

Solve complex theoretical and technical engineering problems by taking a whole systems design cycle approach to: *select and use established engineering methods, techniques, tools and resources, *determine inherent parameters of materials, components and systems by safely carrying out testing and experiments, collecting data, and dealing with sources of error, *interpret, critically analyse, evaluate and synthesise current and emerging information to inform decision-making, *develop and/or model and justify solutions, taking into account potential outcomes, constraints, risks and research-based evidence
Plan, design, construct, test and assess an engineering structure on soil under supervision.
Communicate to a Project Manager in different modes (written, oral and visual) and specified industry formats (e.g. reports, diagrams, client presentations)
Act professionally by: functioning autonomously and in teams, adhering to the engineering code of ethics, demonstrating fundamental management skills

title: Engineering Contracts and Procurement
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of engineering contract principles and procurement strategies, including the legal and ethical considerations involved in contract formation, negotiation, and management.
Reflect on the development of competitive contracts which ensure procurement and stakeholder satisfaction.
Evaluate the critical factors influencing contract development and recommend the best conditions.
Analyse the current market situation and make appropriate predictions relevant to proposed projects.

Develop effective contract management plans, including strategies for monitoring project performance, resolving disputes, and ensuring compliance with contractual obligations, while considering the dynamic nature of engineering projects and evolving industry standards.

Apply advanced analytical skills to evaluate and select appropriate procurement methods and contract types for engineering projects, considering factors such as project scope, risk allocation, cost-effectiveness, and sustainability.

title: Engineering Project Execution
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Interpret modern project management theory and demonstrate relevant practice techniques.
Discuss issues in project management practices with regard to building clients and stakeholders' requirements.
Analyse the application of project management tools and techniques to meet complex contextual demands in different sectors.
Evaluate, analyse, and integrate professional approaches to managing projects within sector specialisations
Apply the latest management tools and techniques for effective and efficient implementation and completion of projects.
Formulate the scope for a project that would be suitable to satisfy stakeholder needs.

title: Advanced Engineering Project 1
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Anne Ng (wng@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and synthesise relevant research literature to gain an in-depth understanding of the current developments in the specific area of the research project to inform the appropriate approach for the engineering research project.

Apply critical and independent thinking to research design, investigation and experimentation to identify gaps in knowledge and synthesise advanced novel engineering solutions that challenge the current state of knowledge and engineering practices.
Analyse and evaluate engineering research data at an advanced level (appropriate to the discipline or advanced field of research).
Apply the ethics, norms and concepts that guide engineering (research) practice (including professionalism, innovation and adaptability).
Design, execute and lead a research project that contributes to the advancement of the engineering discipline and/or field of research.
Recognise the importance of continuous professional development and awareness of the current engineering practice.

title: Advanced Engineering Project 2
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Anne Ng (wng@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Integrate findings from the research project with current research literature to propose innovative engineering solutions and advancements in the chosen specialist domain.

Critically evaluate research project outcomes and performance to generate and justify engineering solutions and future recommendations that are relevant to the discipline and to external stakeholders.
Apply fundamental scientific principles to construct the mathematical, physical, or computational models to analyse and evaluate a major set of engineering data generated during the research project.
Proficiently apply engineering tools and techniques to analyse and visualise research project results, and validate their accuracy.

Prepare a professional research paper (commensurate with the discipline and field of research) to communicate the findings of the dissertation within the engineering profession and to the wider community through written and verbal mediums.

Assess social, legal, environmental contexts and their potential impact on society, and integrate ethics and sustainability in the project design process and when synthesizing engineering solutions based on research project findings.

title: Professional Engineering
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Dariusz Alterman (dalterman@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Recognise the fundamentals applicable to the engineering professional and technologist areas of practice, systems and standards.

Examine the principles and importance of quality management and Workplace, Health and Safety risk management within Australian frameworks, legislation, standards and procedures in the context of the engineering profession.
Apply basic systems engineering and/or project management tools and processes to solve engineering problems.
Apply oral and written communication in a professional engineering and technologist environments and at appropriate levels for technical and general audiences.
Identify where engineers can ethically contribute to society and sustainability.
Demonstrate commitment to life-long learning and professional development through establishment of an ePortfolio

Synthesise and critically evaluate core course concepts and their interrelationships and effectively communicate a comprehensive understanding of the course's main ideas and their broader implications.

title: Integrative Group Project
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Identify the structure, roles and capabilities of the multi-disciplinary engineering team and assign roles and responsibilities accordingly.
Evaluate the feasibility, scope, and potential impact of alternative approaches to conduct the multi-disciplinary research project and justify the best solution.

Critically review and consider the accountabilities of the professional engineer and the project team for the safety of team members, other people and for protection of the environment throughout the project.

Identify and apply the most suitable project management, materials, methods, and data collection techniques for the collaborative research project and integrate these elements into the project design.
Apply understanding of team dynamics and leadership within multi-disciplinary engineering team to coordinate tasks within the team and evaluate alternative viewpoints to achieve project goals.
Identify and address potential ethical dilemmas, ensuring the project adheres to professional and ethical standards.

title: Engineering Project Resource Planning
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Appraise and infer the effective and efficient practices for process monitoring, quality control and assurance.
Critically analyse strategic quality control practices and their application to organisational realities.
Assess team dynamics and reflect on team performance improvement techniques.
Undertake project definition, project planning and project implementation using key tools and techniques for effective project management.
Utilise and engage with the fundamental tools in strategic human resource management including the planning, development, implementation and evaluation of HR activities.

title: Risk Engineering
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Discern and categorise safety and/or financial hazards through standardised, systematic and structured documentation processes.
Critically review engineering and administrative control measures to manage potential risks in engineering projects, including technical, environmental, and safety risks.
Construct models for analysing accidents & consequences through Event Tree Analysis (ETA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) techniques.

Apply advanced risk analysis techniques, including appropriate software tools and methodologies, to model and evaluate risks in order to make informed decisions and optimize risk management strategies.
Apply engineering principles, standards, and best practices to design and implement risk mitigation measures that ensure the safety, reliability, and efficiency of engineering systems.
Cultivate a culture of proactive risk management within engineering projects and integrate risk management principles into all stages of the engineering lifecycle.

title: Engineering System Design
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Rezwanul Haque (rhaque@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles and practices of engineering design required to successfully implement complex engineering solutions.
Investigate and assess scientific material to effectively synthesise relevant information to develop innovative design solutions
Analyse potential failure modes in engineering systems and evaluate their impact to develop strategies to mitigate and prevent failures.
Apply appropriate design concepts to deliver a desired engineering outcome.
Manage time and resources (independently and/or as a member of a team).
Develop Workplace, Health and Safety risk management knowledge and skills, including WHS frameworks, legislation, standards, procedures and guidance.

Synthesise and critically evaluate core course concepts and their interrelationships and effectively communicate a comprehensive understanding of the course's main ideas and their broader implications.

title: Engineering Management
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Dariusz Alterman (dalterman@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of project management principles and techniques, including project scope, risk management, resource allocation, and time management.
Employ a systems engineering approach to analyse complex engineering projects, identifying and integrating key components and subsystems to achieve desired outcomes.
Apply effective estimation and cost management strategies to ensure the successful delivery of engineering projects within budget constraints.
Utilise web-based project management tools to facilitate efficient project planning, tracking, and reporting, while ensuring effective communication and collaboration among team members.
Appraise the ethical, legal, and social implications of engineering management decisions, demonstrating a high level of professional responsibility and integrity.

Develop strong communication and leadership skills to effectively collaborate with project teams, stakeholders, and clients in an engineering management context relevant to a professional engineer and technologist.

Synthesise and critically evaluate core course concepts and their interrelationships and effectively communicate a comprehensive understanding of the course's main ideas and their broader implications.

title: Professional Practice
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:David Alonso-Caneiro (dalonsocaneiro@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Develop Workplace, Health and Safety risk management knowledge and skills, including WHS frameworks, legislation, standards, procedures and guidance.
Report on progress and seek feedback.
Manage available time to achieve workplace assignments.
Function as a member of a professional engineering team.

title: Engineering Innovation and Entrepreneurship
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Frank Washko (fwashko@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Generate concepts in response to an articulated engineering problem using a range of appropriate innovation tools.
Formulate customer requirements leading into a marketing plan to identify targets for technical product commercialisation.
Analyse engineering financial considerations in support of a financial plan.
Integrate all required parts into a full concept Business Plan, such as concept description and management team.
Apply professional written and presentation communications.
Apply concepts of ethics and sustainability where appropriate.

title: Introduction to Sustainable Urban Development & Town Planning
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nayomi Kankanamge (nkankanamge@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Apply the UN Sustainable Development Goals to the processes of urban development and town planning, from the global to the local context.
Communicate the relevant theories, approaches, and data for interdisciplinary and community-led decision-making for sustainable urban development and town planning.

Explore the role that different discipline areas – health, education, science, arts, economics, environment, sociology, engineering, law - all have in shaping and establishing sustainable urban development and town planning.

title: Introduction to Urban Design & Town Planning - Studio I
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Silvia Tavares (stavares@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Describe a range of media and be able to discuss when best to use them.

Understand the different requirements and conventions of urban design-orientated drawing and identify appropriate graphic representation techniques for communicating urban design and town planning concepts.
Identify and use current policies, knowledge, evidence, concepts and theory related to urban design and town planning.

title: Urban Economics and System Analytics
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nicholas Stevens (nstevens@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Describe and discuss contemporary micro and macro planning and property economic theory and the applicability to urban development decision-making.
Reflect on the implications of information and communication technologies and big data for contemporary cities and smart cities.
Demonstrate an understanding of how cities are shaped and transformed through economic, social, technological and environmental interactions and dependencies.
Demonstrate an understanding of visualisations and their usage in a wide variety of applications, including the core skills required to create effective visualisations.

title: Planning Theory, Governance and Politics
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nayomi Kankanamge (nkankanamge@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Understand the nature of spatial planning at all levels of government in Australia.
Reflect on your field trip and practical experience.
Apply theoretical and practical understanding about spatial planning to undertake a practical exercise.

title: Planning and Design for Health and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Greg Mews (gmews@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Demonstrated knowledge of contemporary challenges that are critical to the concepts of urban design and planning for health and wellbeing, healthy communities, and the impact of the environment on human social and biophysical health.
Critique of relevant concepts, policies, and relevant research findings within local and/ or global contexts.
Synthesis of theory, research and frameworks through application within a collaborative context to deepen your understanding and critical self- reflection
Communicate using written, oral and digital media for a range of audience

title: Industry Project 1: Urban Design and Town Planning Studies
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nicholas Stevens (nstevens@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced theoretical and applied urban design and town planning knowledge in a specific research application or learning environment.
Demonstrate an understanding the PIA Code of Conduct and its influence on practice of planning
Conduct research and thinking about social issues that make considered and ethical contributions to the future of society.

title: Urban Climate Theory and Science
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Silvia Tavares (stavares@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Identify climatology principles applied to urban design and town planning
Collect and evaluate urban climate data
Appraise principles of human comfort and health associated with urban climates
Apply solutions for improving urban climate performance
Plan, organise and prepare documents for future reference

title: Regional Transformation:  political and economic geographies
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Jennifer Carter (jcarter@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Explain the theoretical concepts underpinning regional places including rural, urban and peri-urban places and apply them to contemporary contexts
Assess how social, economic and economic geographies interconnect within regional places
Appraise the change processes at local, regional, national and global scales that affect regional development.
Propose potential future directions for regional sustainability and future change.

title: Industry Project 2: Urban Design and Town Planning Studies
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nicholas Stevens (nstevens@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced theoretical and applied social science knowledge in a specific research application or learning environment.
Conduct research and thinking about social issues that make considered and ethical contributions to the future of society.
Demonstrate an understanding the PIA Code of Conduct and its influence on practice of planning

title: Planning and Environmental Law
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nicholas Stevens (nstevens@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Describe and discuss Queenslands Planning Law System
Use online database searches to inform possible development options for individual sites
Apply the provisions of Queenslands Development Assessment system and a local planning scheme in assessing a development proposal
Describe and identify the relationship between planning and other environmental legislation in Queensland
Discuss Queensland Planning appeals system, ADR and the planning enforcement system

title: Public Space Planning and Design - Studio II
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Silvia Tavares (stavares@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe the key concepts and definitions in urban design
Apply the main principles of urban design - looking at the relationships between economic, social and environmental parameters
Synthesise various forms of data to identify problems and opportunities and formulate a vision, goals, objectives and solutions to resolve issues.
Develop and communicate design based solutions which reflect the principles of urban design and respond to requirements of the case study site.
Communicate in a professional manner via verbal, written and graphic media

title: Landscapes, Place and People
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Harriot Beazley (hbeazley@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Apply theories and concepts in international and domestic settings and contexts.
Systematically apply appropriate methods and tools of analysis when analysing issues pertaining to analysis of landscapes, place and people.
Appraise the concepts taught in class with respect to the scales and perspectives of different stakeholders.
Convey concepts studied and researched to other stakeholders.Apply available on-line information and other relevant information to a real world setting.
Offer creative and equitable solutions to current issues and future prospects in analysis of people and place.

title: Culture and Identity in Cities and Regions
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Greg Mews (gmews@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Identify and interpret knowledge associated with spatial justice in the context of culture and identity in cities and regions.

Outline theory, concepts and the need for and use of qualitative and post-qualitative data to decolonise professional planning and design practices by examining the implementation of current strategies.

Perform critical evaluation of contemporary practices and develop a strategy based on creative thinking and doing skills as well as collaborative learning on issues related to culture and identity in cities and regions.
Describe and reflect on personal values and professional practice to demonstrate a capacity to effectively communicate the subject matter.

title: Neighbourhood Planning and Design - Studio III
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nayomi Kankanamge (nkankanamge@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Understand and identify natural and cultural environmental processes; urban and regional economies; and social and demographic parameters.
Recognise and apply relevant planning legislation and policy as it relates to the project site.
Synthesise various forms of data to identify problems and opportunities and formulate objectives and solutions to resolve issues.
Communicate in a professional manner via verbal, written and graphic media

title: Participation and Conflict Resolution
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Greg Mews (gmews@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Apply relevant urban and regional planning (including environment and health) methodologies in the formation of a stakeholder consultation plan

Facilitate and participate in group consultation practices. Effectively use voice, body-language, structure, word choice, graphics, and presentation technology appropriate to the audience. Work effectively as a team member.
Communicate and demonstrate equity, professional practice ethics and consideration of future generations
Explain and describe relevant aspects of sources of conflict and methods of conflict resolution in the planning and environment context
Demonstrate critical analysis of conflict and problem-solving skills in relation to conflict resolution through scenarios/case studies and role plays

title: Advanced Planning Policy and Practice
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Greg Mews (gmews@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Perform critical analysis and demonstrate strategic thinking and Problem solving skills as applied to a diverse range of regional and urban planning issues
Demonstrate knowledge application of suitable Sustainable Development Goals/ New Urban Agenda
Demonstrate a capacity to reflect on personal values and professional practice to inform theory
Demonstrate understanding of planning theory and principles as well as the need for and use of credible information for planning policy and strategy
Effective written communication to appropriate audience

title: Strategic Infrastructure Planning
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nayomi Kankanamge (nkankanamge@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Identify the range of infrastructures that contribute to the operation and facilitation of regional and urban systems.
Identify and describe the issues around supply and demand of infrastructures, including details of a range of demand management strategies.
Carry out research into different infrastructures, link them to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and communicate findings across a range of regional and urban contexts and organisations.
Perform critical analysis and synthesis with both qualitative and quantitative data in reports.

title: Community Planning and Design - Studio IV
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nicholas Stevens (nstevens@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical knowledge and skills to a particular planning context on the Sunshine Coast.

Work as a team member within diverse settings, with commitment to shared goals, team processes and appropriate interpersonal skills, including respect, reliability, mutual supportiveness and time management.
Understand community needs and issues, carry out analysis and present possibilities for solutions back to the community.
Develop creative solutions and plans to deal with community issues.
Effectively communicate with community representatives and professional planners about their planning proposals using written, graphics and verbal communication.

title: Earth's Surface Processes
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Peter Davies (pdavies1@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and apply theoretical and practical knowledge of geological processes and principles to regional and global contexts
Use practical techniques and templates to collect and organise geological information e.g. observation, sampling, laboratory testing, recording

Solve problems in Earth Science by:Analysing and interpreting geological informationIntegrating findings to identify rocks and soils, and constructing geological histories supported by evidence, e.g. diagrams, maps, calculations, observations
Communicate in scientific writing (workbook, reports)

title: Planning Project
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Silvia Tavares (stavares@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Identify how research can contribute to planning theory and practice.
Justify how research process including proposed research methods contributes to solving a planning problem.
Critically analyse literature and use theoretical concepts and empirical data to justify research need, methods, and contribution.
Undertake data gathering according to well-developed methods appropriate to your research question.
Presentation of comprehensive research report.

title: Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Luke Verstraten (lverstra@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate developing-level knowledge of the science of climate change including the main carbon sources and sinks, the characteristics of different greenhouse gases and their influence on global average temperatures and ocean acidity, and their current and trending emissions profile and likely climatic changes that will result.

Demonstrate developing-level knowledge of the concept, principles, and limits of adaptation in relation to impacts from changes in temperature, precipitation, sea-level rise, storm intensity, and ocean acidification on human and natural systems and the be able to articulate factors that determine resilience and adaptive capacity.

Demonstrate developing-level knowledge of the relationship between emissions and different sectors of economies and communities and be able to articulate policies and actions to reduce emissions, enhance sinks, and limit future change.

Demonstrate developing-level knowledge of climate change policy frameworks and other initiatives at different scales and the ethical and practical issues associated with setting and meeting substantive emission reduction targets, adapting to changes, and securing sustainable development.

title: Planning Practicum
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Nicholas Stevens (nstevens@usc.edu.au)School:School of Law and Society
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical and technical planning skills to unfamiliar circumstances
Work in a diverse employment situation requiring application of planning theory, knowledge and skills and reflect on personal values, professional practice and legal and theoretical perspectives
Critique plans, planning tools and built environment proposals
Demonstrate behaviour and knowledge of personal and professional ethical standards

title: Introduction to Environmental Management
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Savindi Caldera (scaldera@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Analyse problems in the context of both local and global influences using systems-based logic and interdisciplinary approaches.
Recognise the importance of natural and cultural assets, biodiversity and ecosystem services as the foundation of economic and societal well-being.

Articulate key environmental and natural resource management objectives at different scales and in different sectors and explain the policies, practices, management systems and legislation relevant to achieving them.

title: Plant Diversity and Ecology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Alison Shapcott (ashapcot@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Understand and explain the key elements of the historical biogeography of Australian plants.
Have knowledge of the major vegetation types in Australia and describe them. Understand the major determinants of vegetation community structure, composition, diversity and distribution.
Be familiar with some of the major plant families in Australia and be able to use a variety of methods to identify plants.
Become familiar with a variety of field methods to study vegetation.
Carry out a field study and undertake data analysis and write a scientific report on the results.

Have an understanding of some of the major adaptations of aquatic and terrestrial plants to their environment. Have an understanding of the reproductive biology and major dispersal mechanisms in plants. Understand the responses to fire of plants.
Understand plant life history variations and population ecology
Have knowledge of angiosperm evolution and speciation

title: Invertebrate Biology and Ecology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Tomer Ventura (tventura@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and apply knowledge about i) diversity & main diagnostic characters of each phylum ii) adaptations to the environment iii) links between form and function iv) the life cycles of parasites and their health and ecological impacts v) ecological roles of invertebrates.
Argue with evidence how the rich diversity of invertebrates and their adaptations seen today are the product of multiple processes in evolution.
Assemble and present a thematic classified collection of invertebrate species that illustrates the diversity of the group and their adaptations to the environment.

title: Environmental Impact Assessment
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Savindi Caldera (scaldera@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Understand the strategic and organisational context of environmental management in different settings and design and deliver practical outcomes that contribute positively to environmental performance.

Synthesise and prioritise information from desktop and field environmental assessments, rank the relative values identified, assess the risks imposed by the development, and determine appropriate environmental management strategies.
Critically evaluate the effectiveness of existing environmental management policies and procedures against relevant criteria and standards.
Articulate and justify specific policies or courses of action on complex environmental issues using discipline based knowledge and established management principles.
Understand and adhere to professional and ethical codes of conduct.

title: Soil Properties, Processes and Rehabilitation
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Peter Davies (pdavies1@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and apply theoretical and practical knowledge of soil processes and principles to regional and global contexts
Use practical techniques and analytical methods to collect and organise soil and sedimentary information e.g. observation, sampling, laboratory testing, recording
Integrate findings to identify, classify and interpret soils and to assess, evaluate and provide recommendations for their rehabilitation
Communicate findings through scientific reports and seminars.

title: Earth Observation: Remote Sensing and Surveying
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Sanjeev Srivastava (ssrivast@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Describe, explain and assess geospatial techniques and concepts.
Select and apply geospatial tools and skills to address a real-world issue
Evaluate and justify the use of different primary earth observation datasets for different applications.
Demonstrate critical spatial thinking

title: Coastal and Marine Ecology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Ben Gilby (bgilby@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively and professionally to informed audiences.
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of major marine ecosystems and the forces that shape marine biodiversity.
Critically analyse and evaluate field data to investigate basic ecological patterns in coastal ecosystems.
Work as a group to communicate complex scientific principles simply

title: Terrestrial Vertebrate Diversity and Ecology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Dominique Potvin (dpotvin@usc.edu.au)School:School of Science, Technology and Engineering
learning_outcomes: Apply and demonstrate knowledge of diversity, ecology and evolution of wildlife in various contexts. Building disciplinary and interdisciplinary knowledge through a scholarly approach incorporating global and regional perspectives (Professional Standards mapping)
Conduct scientific research using field and ecology data analysis skills - having both the capacity and confidence to pursue the attainment of full potential (Professional Standards mapping)
Communicate in the style of a formal scientific poster - having both the capacity and confidence to pursue the attainment of full potential (Professional Standards mapping)
Identify and apply ethical principles to wildlife research - acting with integrity in intellectual, professional and community pursuits (Professional Standards mapping)

title: Weather and Climate

title: Introduction to Nutrition
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Clare Dix (cdix@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Nutrition and Dietetics

learning_outcomes: Understand and explain the theories that underpin the study of human development
Critically analyse issues and research conducted in developmental psychology
Demonstrate a clear and concise argument that is supported by psychological research, alone and with peers.

title: Social Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kay Pozzebon (kpozzebo@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Explain concepts, theories, and research relating to the study of social psychology.
Explain and apply social psychology and cultural responsiveness to individuals, groups, and issues.
Discuss and evaluate the scientific method and methodological issues.
Communicate knowledge appropriately for the psychology discipline.

title: Interpersonal and Group Skills
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kristen Tulloch (ktulloch@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Explain major theoretical, empirical and cultural concepts in interpersonal communication
Apply major theoretical, empirical and cultural concepts in interpersonal communication to real-life scenarios relevant to industry or research.
Reflect upon and analyse your own interpersonal communication to identify areas for personal skill development.
Develop coherent arguments that can be supported by relevant research literature.
Demonstrate proficiency in a qualitative methodology

title: Motivation and Emotion
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Rachael Sharman (rsharman@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Understand and explain the major theories and concepts of human motivation and emotion, and to recognise and explain how these factors influence human behaviour.
Consider and participate in self-exploration to develop a deeper understanding of the theory of motivation and emotion.
Transfer knowledge of human motivation and emotion to applied concepts and scenarios.
Develop appropriate strategies and interventions to overcome a variety of motivational problems.
Develop coherent arguments that can be supported by relevant research literature.

title: Research Methods and Analysis 2
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kay Pozzebon (kpozzebo@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Explain and distinguish between a variety of research methods used in psychological research.
Describe the ethical principles and practices employed in psychological research.
Explain the concepts of levels of measurement, sampling, and reliability and validity including how they apply to psychological research.
Explain and interpret the key features and concepts of descriptive and inferential statistics.
Apply basic functions and applications using statistical software.
Communicate information appropriately for the psychology discipline.

title: Intercultural and Indigenous Psychologies
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Barnaby Dixson (bdixson@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Understand and explain the socio-cultural bases of human behaviour
Critically evaluate intercultural and Indigenous psychological research
Demonstrate an appreciation of cultural and linguistic diversity and develop an appreciation of intercultural communication skills
Demonstrate an appreciation of the effects of culture on one's thought and actions

title: Advanced Methods in Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Daniel Fassnacht (dfassnacht@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of a range of statistical techniques used in psychological research.
Demonstrate knowledge and competence of relevant statistical software.
Select and apply statistical techniques appropriate for the analysis of specific psychological data.
Justify the selection and use of appropriate statistical techniques.
Write and present research findings in a scientific fashion.

title: Personality and Assessment
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Varghese Peter (vpeter@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Understand and explain theories relating to the study of personality and psychological assessment (including ethical issues).
Analyse, synthesise, apply and critically evaluate information.
Develop writing skills, including referencing in APA style.

title: Cognitive and Perceptual Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Odette Norton (onorton@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Understand core and advanced research paradigms, theories and concepts in cognitive and perceptual psychology
Critically evaluate research in cognitive and perceptual psychology.
Apply scientific knowledge to everyday cognitive and perceptual functioning.
Present a clear, coherent and independent exposition of knowledge and ideas.

title: Human Associative Learning
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Odette Norton (onorton@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply core and advanced research paradigms in human associative learning
Critically evaluate research and research data in specific populations
Select and apply scientific knowledge to everyday human associative learning issues
Present information in a clear and concise manner in appropriate style

title: Psychological Disorders
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Mathew Summers (msummers@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate in depth understanding of the history and philosophy of psychological disorders.

Demonstrate in depth understanding of core concepts in the field of psychological disorders, including (1) symptoms, (2) aetiology, (3) assessment and clinical formulations, and (4) evidence-based treatments.
Transfer and adapt knowledge to applied contexts.
Critically evaluate relevant psychological research.
Critically apply knowledge of diversity and the impact of social, cultural, historical and professional influences on practice related to psychological disorders.
Present a clear, coherent and independent exposition of knowledge and ideas.

title: Psychology of Health and Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Angela Hinz (ahinz@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Research and describe strategies for explaining and changing health risk and health enhancing behaviour.
Understand the role of psychology in health and wellbeing.
Critically evaluate health psychology research and develop arguments that can be supported by relevant research literature.
Describe major concepts and theoretical approaches related to the biological and psychosocial determinants of health and wellbeing.
Demonstrate an appreciation of diversity and the impact of culture and context with regard to the psychology of health and wellbeing.

title: Research Methods and Analysis 4
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Joshua Adie (jadie1@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of a range of advanced research designs and methodologies used in psychological research.
Demonstrate appropriate use of multivariate statistical techniques for the analysis of psychological data.
Apply multivariate quantitative techniques and qualitative techniques and to the analysis of psychological data.
Write and present complex research findings in a scientific fashion.
Demonstrate competence in the use of appropriate statistical programs for analysis of psychological data.
Demonstrate knowledge and application of Bayes theorem and statistical techniques in psychological research

title: Advanced Theoretical Issues in Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Prudence Millear (pmillear@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Articulate and explain the theoretical perspectives that are central to the science and practice of psychology, highlighting the relative strengths and limitations of these perspectives.
Demonstrate critical evaluation of the research literature and associated research methods, observations, and theoretical developments.
Consider and evaluate future directions in the field of psychology and potential applied applications.
Demonstrate understanding and responsiveness to culturally and linguistically diverse populations and critical analysis of relevant literature

title: Professional Practice of Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Daniel Fassnacht (dfassnacht@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate professional and ethical practice regarding the rights of clients who participate in a psychological assessment or intervention
Comprehend, explain, and select from a range of psychological assessment techniques
Demonstrate appropriate listening and verbal interaction skills when interacting with a client including awareness of diverse cultural backgrounds
Understand and appreciate the social and cultural factors that might influence the outcome of a psychological assessment
Create a case formulation from client interview data and communicate your findings

title: Adult Development and Ageing
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Prudence Millear (pmillear@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Critically research and evaluate major theoretical and empirical perspectives on human ageing and wellbeing and apply to ageing in diverse populations and situations.
Apply the lifespan developmental approach to ageing in a critical research project and to develop an intervention using contemporary research to promote successful aging.
Demonstrate understanding and responsiveness to culturally and linguistically diverse populations and critical analysis of relevant literature

title: Ethical and Professional Issues In Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Helen Hall (hhall1@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the Psychology Board Code of Conduct and associated Guidelines regarding the practice of psychology.
Demonstrate knowledge of the major ethical issues confronting psychologists in professional practice.
Apply that knowledge to analyse and formulate responses in hypothetical practice situations.
Apply ethical decision making approaches to the formulation and analysis of ethical dilemmas across the lifespan in empirically valid and culturally responsive ways.

title: Advanced Psychological Assessment and Reporting
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Celine Jona (cjona@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Show knowledge and understanding of current research and theory in the field of clinical assessment and psychometrics.
Show knowledge of the information required to select relevant assessment procedures and psychological tests.

Demonstrate appropriate administration, scoring and interpretation of the major psychological tests commonly used in psychological practice to competently and ethically apply evidence‐based and scientific methods to professional practice across the lifespan in empirically valid and culturally responsive ways
Show knowledge of and competence in the procedures involved in writing effective psychological assessment reports.

Show awareness of the limitations and common misconceptions in psychological testing. Show awareness and use of ethical issues using the APS Code of Ethics and its accompanying Guidelines to resolve ethical questions.

title: Advanced and Transcultural Counselling
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kathryn Esparza (kesparza@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and use of advanced counselling skills.
Show knowledge and understanding of the key role of the working alliance in effective psychological consultations of all types and skills for developing an effective working alliance.

Show knowledge and understanding of the difficulties inherent in psychological consultations involving attention to cultural issues, and skills for delivering effective transcultural psychological interventions, particularly with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island People and refugees.
Show awareness of potential ethical issues in psychological practice and an understanding of how to align practice with the AHPRA Code of Conduct, particularly in transcultural consultations.

title: Clinical Psychological Practice 1
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Lee Kannis-Dymand (lkannisd@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Show strong knowledge of and skills in accessing the published empirical findings regarding psychological theories and models for a range of adult psychological disorders.
Show competency, knowledge of and skills in the use of the major methods of diagnostic and assessment procedures.
Show competency, knowledge of and skills in designing and implementing appropriate evidence-based psychological and pharmacological interventions.

Show awareness of potential ethical issues involved in practising clinical psychology and understanding of how to use the APS Code of Ethics and its accompanying Guidelines to resolve ethical questions.
Demonstrate competence in communicating knowledge and skills effectively in writing and through verbal communication

title: Research Dissertation
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Daniel Fassnacht (dfassnacht@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and to evaluate advanced theoretical knowledge in the core area of psychology in which they have chosen to undertake their dissertation
Apply critical analysis to investigate research literature to formulate hypotheses and design a research method to suitably test the hypotheses.
Demonstrate competence in the preparation and submission of an ethics proposal and in ethical conduct of research project
Demonstrate competence in gathering, analysing and reporting research data relevant to a set of research predictions.
Demonstrate competence to develop, organise, and produce a substantial psychology-based research report

title: Practicum Placement 1
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Andrew Allen (aallen2@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competency with knowledge and skills required to work as a clinical psychologist.
Demonstrate competency/ strong knowledge and skills in the design and implementation of clinical psychological interventions.
Demonstrate competency/strong knowledge and skills in dealing professionally with clients and with other professionals.
Demonstrate competency in ability to communicate knowledge and skills effectively in writing and through oral presentation.

Demonstrate strong knowledge of ethical, legal and professional aspects of psychological practice and understanding of using the APS Code of Ethics and its accompanying Guidelines, and other relevant sources, to resolve ethical questions.
Demonstrate behaviour consistent with the legal requirements and code of conduct relevant to psychologists.

title: Advanced Research Design and Methods
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kathina Ali (kali@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding of recent developments in clinical research methodology and design.

Demonstrate an ability to access and, critique methodological strategies relevant to clinical research, and the ability to present, compare and contrast such methodologies in a cogent manner through professional presentations and materials.
Demonstrate understanding and responsiveness to diverse populations and critical analysis of relevant literature.

title: Clinical Psychological Practice 2
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kirstie Daken (kdaken@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and skill in accessing the research findings regarding the psychopathology of a range of child, adolescent and adult psychological disorders.
Demonstrate knowledge and skills in the use of relevant diagnostic, assessment, and treatment procedures.
Demonstrate knowledge and skills in accessing and applying appropriate evidence-based therapy.

Demonstrate awareness of potential ethical issues involved in practising clinical psychology and understanding of how to use the APS Code of Ethics and its accompanying Guidelines to resolve ethical questions.
Ability to synthesise and communicate psychological findings

title: Research Project 1
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Lee Kannis-Dymand (lkannisd@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology

Present psychological evidence to support proposed study.

Show awareness of potential ethical issues involved in psychological research and understanding of and practice in using the AHPRA Psychology Board's Code of Conduct and other relevant sources to resolve ethical questions
Communicate research and justify and interpret theoretical propositions, methodologies, findings and conclusions.

title: Human Associative Learning
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kate Mulgrew (kmulgrew@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health and Behavioural Sciences
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply core and advanced research paradigms in human associative learning
Critically evaluate research and research data for use with specific populations
Select and apply advanced knowledge and well-developed judgement to complex associative learning issues
Present knowledge in a clear and concise manner in appropriate style

Transfer core and advanced knowledge of human motivation and emotion to applied concepts and scenarios.

Develop coherent arguments that can be supported by relevant research literature.

learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competency with knowledge and skills required to work as a psychologist.

title: Ethics and Professional Practice of Psychology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kathina Ali (kali@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology

Show awareness of potential ethical problems that arise in working with vulnerable populations, including individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds.
Demonstrate knowledge of the contribution of other professions and ability to effectively collaborate with multidisciplinary professions in the context of psychology.
Show engagement in self-reflective practice in the context of own values and beliefs and recognition of impact on professional practice.

title: Clinical Psychological Practice 3
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Andrew Allen (aallen2@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Show knowledge of and practice in accessing the research findings regarding the psychopathology of a range of psychological disorders and psychological interventions across the lifespan.
Show knowledge of diagnostic and assessment procedures.
Show knowledge of and competence in application of appropriate evidence-based therapy.
Show awareness of potential ethical issues involved in practising clinical psychology.
Show cultural awareness and responsiveness in the assessment, diagnosis, formulation and treatment of relevant psychological disorders.

learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced knowledge, skills and competencies required to work as a psychologist.

title: Research Project 2

title: Clinical Health Psychology and Psychopharmacology
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kirstie Daken (kdaken@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of and practice in accessing research regarding the role of psychological factors in the aetiology of and reactions to illness and health maintenance
Demonstrate knowledge of and practice in the use of relevant assessment procedures
Demonstrate knowledge of and practice in accessing and applying appropriate evidence-based interventions

Demonstrate knowledge regarding the nature, modes of action, effects and side-effects of drugs, recreational, social and therapeutic, and an understanding of pharmacotherapy, to facilitate effective communication with medical carers.

Show awareness of potential ethical issues involved in practising clinical psychology and an understanding of how to use the APS Code of Ethics and its accompanying Guidelines to resolve ethical questions
Demonstrate logical reasoning skills and objectivity in clinical decision making

title: Introduction to Physiotherapy Practice A
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Cherie Wells (cwells@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Physiotherapy
learning_outcomes: Describe the scope of practice and role of physiotherapists within different settings and identify opportunities for physiotherapy interventions and collaboration with other professions
Explain the professional, ethical, legal and registration requirements to practice physiotherapy in Australia, and implications for students and graduates
Demonstrate a safe, person-centred, and culturally sensitive approach to interviewing clients and conducting physical assessments of pain, movement and function
Demonstrate effective communication skills, critical reflection, and ability to give and receive feedback in a professional manner within academic and clinical contexts
Begin to observe, assess, describe, and document the movement, posture, and function of clients across the lifespan using appropriate anatomical terms and professional language
Apply the International Classification of Functioning and Disability model to physiotherapy assessment and clinical reasoning through findings to identify client strengths, challenges and priorities

title: Introduction to Physiotherapy Practice B
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Pierre Roscher (proscher@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Physiotherapy
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a safe, effective, and sensitive approach to assessing symptoms, range of movement, muscle length, muscle strength, and function
Apply clinical reasoning skills and knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and psychology to identify factors contributing to movement impairments and implications for treatment
Deliver prescribed exercises in a safe and effective manner to reduce symptoms, improve range of movement, muscle length, muscle strength and function
Safely implement screening tools, therapy and exercise programs prescribed by allied health professionals and monitor the health status and response of clients
Critically reflect on learning and client needs, recognise personal and professional limitations and seek help and assistance as required
Communicate clearly, professionally, and ethically and complete clinical documentation and administrative duties in a timely and effective manner

title: Research Project 3
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Lee Kannis-Dymand (lkannisd@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Select and apply quantitative (statistical) or qualitative techniques for data analysis
Interpretation of results

Show further awareness of potential ethical issues involved in psychological research and understanding of and practice in using AHPRA Psychology Board's Code of Conduct and other relevant sources to resolve ethical questions

title: Core Physiotherapy Skills A
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Olivia Galea (ogalea@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Physiotherapy
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective, culturally safe and respectful communication and complete clinical documentation in a timely and accurate manner
Describe the clinical presentation, assessment, evidence-based treatment and prevention of different types of orthopaedic and sports injuries, and implications for physiotherapy
Comply with professional, occupational health and safety requirements, identify and manage risks, and work in a safe, ethical and responsible manner with other health professionals
Apply massage, taping, braces/supports, and prescribe exercise in a safe and client-centred manner under the supervision of a suitably qualified health professional
Critically reflect on learning, skills and capacity, and work safely within scope of practice as an allied health assistant, sports trainer or physiotherapy student

title: Research Project 4
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Lee Kannis-Dymand (lkannisd@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Complete a substantial research project
Describe limitations and future implications of the findings of the project
Demonstrate advanced clear and articulate communication

title: Core Physiotherapy Skills B

learning_outcomes: Explain the role of physiotherapists and other health professionals in the assessment and management of clients with orthopaedic conditions
Assess client symptoms, movement, balance and gait, and provide education, exercise and gait aids to optimise recovery, function, and prevent falls
Educate and assist a client to safely mobilise with gait aids after orthopaedic surgery or injury, and progress or regress gait as indicated
Demonstrate ethical and professional behaviour, critical reflection skills and a commitment to client-centred care, evidence-based practice and lifelong learning
Work safely within scope and demonstrate effective communication, documentation and inter-professional collaboration
Screen contraindications and precautions, and safely apply and justify the use of electrophysical agents in different clinical contexts

title: Practicum Placement 4
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Kathryn Esparza (kesparza@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Psychology
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced practice and application of clinical psychological procedures in the workplace;

Deal professionally with clients and with other professionals.

Demonstrate skills in and awareness of self-reflective practice including the capacity to reflect on placement experiences and performance to improve clinical practice.

title: Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Cherie Wells (cwells@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Physiotherapy
learning_outcomes: Assess and treat physiotherapy clients with cardiorespiratory disorders in a safe, effective, client-centred, and evidence-based manner
Apply effective clinical reasoning to plan and interpret client assessments, and to select, justify and modify treatments
Describe clinical features of common cardiorespiratory conditions and explain the role of different health professionals in diagnosis, assessment and treatment
Demonstrate ethical, legal and professional behaviour in clinical contexts and work within personal and professional scope of practice
Effectively communicate and collaborate with different health professionals and complete clinical documentation in an accurate and efficient manner

title: Neurological Physiotherapy
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Cherie Wells (cwells@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Physiotherapy
learning_outcomes: Plan and conduct physiotherapy assessment and treatment of clients with neurological disorders in a safe, effective, and evidence-based manner
Apply critical thinking, analytical skills and clinical reasoning to identify client problems and priorities, and to justify and modify assessments and treatments
Describe common neurological disorders and pathology, and explain the role of physiotherapy and other health professionals in assessment and treatment
Comply with ethical and legal requirements, work safely within scope and capabilities, and seek help when needed in clinical contexts
Demonstrate respectful, flexible and effective communication and collaboration with clients and other health professionals and timely and accurate documentation

assessment_tasks.task_name: Objective Structured Clinical Examination 1 - Neurological Assessment

title: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy A

Apply effective communication, interprofessional collaboration and documentation skills within clinical contexts
Conduct subjective and objective assessments of clients with peripheral musculoskeletal disorders in a safe, effective, and client-centred manner

Apply evidence-based physiotherapy treatments for peripheral musculoskeletal disorders in a safe, effective and client-centred manner
Monitor client response and outcomes to peripheral musculoskeletal assessment and treatment and adjust approach or refer to other health professionals as indicated

Conduct subjective and objective musculoskeletal assessments of the spine, pelvis and ribcage in a safe, effective and client-centred manner
Clinically reason through musculoskeletal assessments to generate a diagnosis and problem list, and to plan and justify treatment and reassessment
Apply evidence-based treatments for musculoskeletal disorders of the spine, pelvis, and ribcage in a safe, effective and client-centred manner
Monitor client response and outcomes to physiotherapy assessment and treatment and adjust approach or refer to other health professionals as indicated

title: Paediatric Physiotherapy
syllabus_overview: Course Coordinator:Cherie Wells (cwells@usc.edu.au)School:School of Health - Physiotherapy
learning_outcomes: Plan and conduct subjective and objective assessments of paediatric clients with diverse presentations in a safe, effective, and client-centred manner
Demonstrate knowledge and skills in treating paediatric clients with diverse presentations in a safe, effective, and client-centred manner

Communicate effectively with peers, clients, family, and health professionals to optimise client care and to provide high quality education regarding physiotherapy
Comply with ethical, legal, and professional requirements when assessing and treating paediatric clients, and complete accurate and timely clinical documentation

title: Physiotherapy for Aging and Disability

Explore a client's functioning and disability using the International Classification of Functioning and Disability and use this information to guide clinical reasoning
Design an evidence-based exercise and education program to assist a client to safely manage their chronic medical condition and reduce their level of disability
Demonstrate skills in assessing and treating clients who are aging and/or have a disability due to a chronic medical condition in a safe and effective manner

Understand procedures involved in assessing microbial and chemical risks associated with food.

Apply knowledge of risk principles and prescribed food safety standards to evaluate food safety programs and design of food premises.
